links.outcome: Fixed-horizon AUROC of ML survival model versus physician estimates and 1995 model
links.effect: At 60 days AUROC was 0.750 for the survival model, 0.808 for physicians (matched sample) and 0.827 for the 1995 model; gap reproduced across eight splits.
links.quote: The survival model achieved a competitive ranking concordance (0.705) but underperformed both comparators at fixed horizons: at 60 days its area under the ROC curve was 0.750, versus 0.808 for physicians (on the matched sample) and 0.827 for the 1995 model, a gap reproduced across eight independent splits and statistically reliable after multiplicity correction.

links.outcome: Concordance index versus timepoint-specific discrimination as evaluation metrics
links.effect: Concordance was competitive (0.705) but 60-day AUROC was 0.750, below comparators (0.808, 0.827); recalibration did not change discrimination.
links.quote: The survival model achieved a competitive ranking concordance (0.705) but underperformed both comparators at fixed horizons: at 60 days its area under the ROC curve was 0.750, versus 0.808 for physicians (on the matched sample) and 0.827 for the 1995 model, a gap reproduced across eight independent splits and statistically reliable after multiplicity correction.

links.outcome: Discrimination across sex, race, and age subgroups
links.effect: Discrimination was reported as equitable across sex, race, and age subgroups.
links.quote: Discrimination was equitable across sex, race, and age.

links.outcome: Generalization to disease groups absent from training (leave-one-disease-out validation)
links.effect: Severe generalization failure in disease groups absent from training.
links.quote: Leave-one-disease-out validation revealed severe generalization failure in disease groups absent from training.

screen.reason: Evaluates ML survival models against physician judgment and logistic models for ICU mortality prediction, specifically demonstrating pitfalls of ranking-optimized models for fixed-horizon bedside tasks and evaluating validation strategies (leave-one-subgroup) and objective alignment.

primary.practice: timepoint-matched training vs ranking optimization and leave-one-subgroup validation
